thread.title: Tech Today: Micron Rallies, Facebook's Insta-charm, Bully for Qorvo

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: Micron Rallies, Facebook's Insta-charm, Bully for Qorvo
text:
Here are some things going on today in the world of tech:
Micron rallies, brushing off China worry Shares of memory-chip titan Micron Technology ( MU ) are up $1.52, or 3%, at $53, after the company this morning confirmed it was notified of a temporary injunction banning some sales of its parts in China but said that the ban won't hurt its results for the August-ending fiscal Q4 , given that the ban covers products that make up only about 1% of Micron's sales.
Two things were being discussed by the Street in the 36 hours or so since the story of the ban first broke on Tuesday . One is how this may boost prices for DRAM chips, a good thing for Micron, and the other is about how this is merely one move in the ongoing tariff and trade battle between China and the U.S.
Before Micron's announcement this morning, RBC Capital 's Amit Daryanani , who has an Overweight rating on Micron shares, wrote that "we could see this injunction if accurate keep DRAM prices elevated on a global level - especially considering the injunction could skew global supply/demand heading into a seasonally strong Sept-qtr for DRAM, though on NAND side it could be a modest negative for MU."
And Stifel 's Kevin Cassidy , also writing before the announcement, opined that "China's goal may not be to block shipments of Micron's much needed DRAM but instead part of a strategy to push Micron toward partnering with China semiconductor foundries " in order to speed up China's own chip-industry development.
As far as the announcement this morning, Shebly Seyrafi of FBN Securities writes that today will be all about a "relief rally" in the shares, as is clearly the case.
Seyrafi also points out that data from the DRAMeXchange shows that some prices for " solid-state drives " using NAND flash chips "actually increased to $119.71 on June 29th from $118.41 on May 25th," which shows "Micron is actually experiencing a price improvement on the Crucial SSD."
Trade hangs over chip conference Speaking of chips and trade, Cowen & Co. 's Krish Sankar today previews the Semicon West conference that kicks off Tuesday in downtown San Francisco, and he expects trade to be an overhang for the show, particularly for chip-equipment makers such as Applied Materials ( AMAT ) and Lam Research ( LRCX ).
"An incremental risk that has been noted recently includes potential export controls on SPE tools to China," writes Sankar, referring to expectations the Trump administration will impose limits on what can be sold to China.
"Given the very fluid state of trade negotiations, we believe it is difficult to handicap the various outcomes due to the political nature of this issue," he writes. "At Semicon West, we do not expect any company management teams to offer resolutions to these questions nor are we expecting any earnings outlook adjustments related to China trade."
The other issue will be the effect of mixed trends in Micron's memory-chip market, including declining prices for NAND flash. Sankar believes that's mostly "in the stocks" of the equipment makers at this point. But see last week's piece by Needham & Co .'s Edwin Mok for a more dire view.
Qorvo's opportunity expands Shares of wireless chip vendor Qorvo ( QRVO ) are up $3.27, or 4%, at $80.71, after KeyBanc 's John Vinh this morning raised his rating on the shares to Overweight from Sector Weight and assigned a $95 price target, after concluding that it's " time to buy mobile ."
Vinh is encouraged about trends in China's smartphone buying, and sees Apple 's ( AAPL ) iPhone sales " stabilizing ."
China's sales of smartphones, he's hearing, exhibit "consistently positive demand trends," with "most supply-chain partners indicating strong demand in the 2Q of 10-15% q/q growth as demand began to improve in April with momentum continuing into May, which was particularly strong.
"Expectations are that q/q growth can be sustained into the 3Q, which is expected to grow 10-15% q/q."
Apple's iPhone 8 and iPhone X demand "appears to have stabilized ahead of the new iPhone cycle," he adds, and Qorvo looks likely to gain additional business in this year's updated iPhones, he writes, selling the "Super PAD," the "antenna tuning" circuitry, and the "envelope tracking" chips.
Facebook's Instagram sizzles Shares of Facebook (FB) are up $3.37, or 1.8%, at $196.07, after BTIG 's Rich Greenfield this morning hiked his price target on the shares to $275 from $175, after concluding that the company's advertising opportunity is "exciting," and that despite all the controversy around the company-see Tuesday's headlines about the FBI getting into the action-"consumers could not care less" because they "love Facebook and all of its key services."
Getty Images Greenfield focuses on Instagram , the photo-sharing property, which "has become an absolute monster." He thinks Instagram has achieved the Holy Grail of advertising, making advertising feel like "content": "People love the ads," on Instagram, he contends, "allowing for greater load and higher CPMs."
"The ads are so good in fact, that Instagram is quickly becoming the most powerful and valuable mall in the world," writes Greenfield, "where you not only browse, but can buy anything you see." Greenfield raises his estimates for this year and 2019 and 2020. His 2018 numbers go to $57.3 billion in revenue and $35.6 billion in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, or Ebitda, up from $51.1 billion and $31.4 billion respectively.
Greebfield writes that "$275 equates to a multiple of 17x 2019 estimated EBITDA and a 2019 P/E of 24x, neither of which feels aggressive given Facebook's continued growth, not to mention, operating expense growth and capital investment levels feel unsustainably high."
For more, see my colleague David Marino-Nachison 's piece on the matter.
As regards the FBI/SEC/FTC/DoJ investigation, Monness Crespi Hardt 's Brian White writes this morning that he was expecting such "aftershocks" after the Cambridge Analytica matter.
At this point, he argues, "we believe the shock value of this scandal is already reflected in the stock ," given that Facebook shares fetch "just 20 times our calendar 2019 EPS projection (ex-cash) for a company that we are projecting 40% revenue growth in 2018 with 43% EPS growth."
Alibaba can survive currency shifts MKM Partners ' Rob Sanderson this morning pounds the table for shares of Alibaba Group Holding (BABA), reiterating a Buy rating and a $280 price target, writing that the stock is being unduly punished because of a recent devaluation of China's currency .
Since it went public, Alibaba has suffered through five separate incidences of decline in the yuan against the dollar, Sanderson observes.
"We think this is another such event," referring to the fact that "over the past two weeks, the Yuan has declined 3.7% vs. the dollar and the stock is down 11% (v NASDAQ down 3%).
"With nearly all of the business related to Chinese domestic consumption and negligible U.S. cross-border activity, exposure is really just currency translation and valuation should more closely mirror exchange rates.
"In every f/x volatility event to date, the stock has seen a much greater recovery than the initial retreat once exchange rates stabilize. We would take advantage of recent weakness and accumulate the stock."
Alibaba shares today are down 56 cents at $184.19.
